Last Friday (21st), following the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case, in the early hours of the morning, police escorted a woman who was queuing for a courtroom seat into a police vehicle and took her away. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges, including "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or deliberately obstructing police officers in the execution of their duties", and "seditious intent".

At approximately 5 a.m. last Friday, over 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of wearing a shirt with some seditious intent", and took her into a police vehicle and drove her away. When officers led the woman away, several officers continuously directed reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and extended the orange cordon towards YING WA STREET direction. Once the woman had boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon. On that day, a "court observation volunteer" who was queuing near the woman said that she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

Collective (集誌社) enquired with the police about the reasons for the woman being taken away and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this (24th) morning that a security operation had been carried out in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Court on 21 August, during which a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or deliberately obstructing police officers in the execution of their duties", and "seditious intent", and was being detained for investigation.
